updates.rationale: Immutable action inputs prevent later re-approval from invalidating authorized work; explicit batch authorization keeps repairs reviewable.
updates.statement: Combination-only defects may be repaired directly in a batch under the actor, source, timestamp and initial members recorded by batch-open. Final lists those commits, subjects, diffstats and authorization for review; no batch-owned change or journal ceremony is required. Member defects stay in members and conflict continuation is unchanged. Schema-1 batches retain parent-approved batch-owned change authority.

updates.rationale: Immutable action inputs prevent later re-approval from invalidating authorized work; explicit batch authorization keeps repairs reviewable.
updates.statement: The existing reference-transaction hook judges each implementation commit from that commit and its parent, using the same attribution function as final and the member predicate used by ready. Later re-approval never changes earlier verdicts. Member tip packages must be approved and each must have covered implementation, without requiring implementation after re-approval. Hook installation and missing-engine behavior remain unchanged in this member.

decisions.reason: Owner approved structural plan proposals A, B, F1 and F4. PyReduce history showed tip-based re-approval retroactively invalidating approved work and excluded drafts adding ceremony. Immutable commit and parent inputs give hook and final one verdict; a side ledger would be incomplete and mutable. Batch authorization explicitly owns combination repairs rather than claiming member contracts. Reopen if immutable history cannot supply authority or review fails to expose repairs. M3 owns subsequent hook installation and engine identity changes.
